data.item: KCB Group stepped into 2021 with renewed optimism of doing better than the previous year. This confidence was informed by the deliberate initiatives that we undertook to ring-fence our business in 2020, support our customers and other stakeholders as well as guarantee the safety and wellbeing of our staff. At the onset of the pandemic, we took concerted efforts to conserve our capital, manage liquidity and contain our costs. These steps enabled us to enter the second year of the pandemic from a position of strength granting us the power to drive our plans. Our Beyond Banking strategy which is on its second last year remains anchored on delivering the very best in customer experience and driving a digital future. In anticipation of a stronger year ahead, and a more sustainable recovery, we are deepening our focus on supporting various sectors of the economy as we walk with our customers to regain their lost foothold due to the COVID-19 crisis. We also made strategic investments to deepen our regional play while building a sustainable business for the future that is anchored on people, planet, and profit. 42

data.item: zaidi, Kundi la KCB liliingia mwaka wa 2021 na matumaini mapya ya kufanya vyema kuliko mwaka uliotangulia. Imani yetu ilichangiwa na mikakati tuliyoiweka kuikinga biashara yetu mwaka 2020, kuwasaidia wateja wetu, wadau wengine na kuhakikisha usalama na afya ya wafanyakazi wetu. Mwanzoni mwa janga, tulichukua hatua za kuhifadhi mtaji wetu, kudhibiti mzunguko wa fedha na gharama zetu. Hatua hizi zilituwezesha kungia mwaka wa pili wa janga tukiwa imara zaidi. Hili lilitupatia nguvu ya kuendeleza mipango yetu. Mkakati wetu wa Zaidi ya Benki, ambao upo katika mwaka wa pili sasa, unasalia kuangazia utoaji wa huduma bora zaidi kwa wateja na kuongoza siku kidijitali za usoni. Kwa kutarajia mwaka mwema mbele yetu, na kuendelea kujikwamua, tunakoleza juhudi zetu katika kuangazia kusaidia sekta mbalimbali za uchumi tunapotembea na wateja wetu katika safari yetu ya kujirejesha tena katika hali tuliyokuwa kabla ya janga la COVID-19 kutokea. Tumefanya pia uwekezaji wa busara kwa lengo la kukoleza mchango wetu katika kanda huku tukijenga biashara endelevu kwa ajili ya siku zijazo yenye msingi wake katika watu, dunia na faida. 46

Nafuu ya kisheria kifedha. Faida ya Kundi kabla ya ushuru Agosti 2021, ya muda wa kulipa mikopo kwa wateja iliongezeka zaidi ya maradufu mwaka 2021. tulikamilisha ununuzi walioathiriwa sana, kwa mfano, ilimalizika Faida baada ya ushuru ilifikia KShs 34.2 bilioni wa Banque Populaire katika kanda isipokuwa kwa sekta za hoteli na ukilinganisha na KShs 19.6 bilioni, ongezeko elimu nchini Uganda. Ingawa baadhi ya hatua la 74%, kutokana na ongezeko la mapato na du Rwanda (BPR). Hii iliwezesha wafanyakazi ya kutoongeza gesi ya mkaa na utekelezaji Kujenga Nembo kuu ya Kanda wetu kurejea kazini 100% katika biashara wa Malengo ya Maendeleo Endelevu (SDG). Mwaka 2014 KCB ilianza juhudi za kuiboresha zetu zote kufikia Desemba 2021. Kadhalika, uwezeshaji wa wafanyakazi wetu nembo yake kuwa muwezeshaji wa biashara wanaoangazia ukopeshaji katika mabadiliko ili kukidhi mahitaji ya wateja. Mabadiliko Na 2021, tulikamilisha kuunda Kamati ya tabia nchi na mazingira. haya yalituwezesha kujilainisha na masoko Kuu Tendaji baada ya kuthibitishwa kwa na kusaidia utimizaji wa mkakati wa Bernard Okello kama Mkurugenzi wa Nikihitimisha, ningependa kuwashukuru Benki kupitia lengo lililoelezwa vyema la Mikopo wa Kundi na uteuzi wa Rosalind wafanyakazi wetu wote kwa kujitolea kwao (Kurahisisha Ulimwengu wako Kukuwezesha Gichuru kama Mkurugenzi wa Kundi wa wakati wa janga. Ni kupitia tu juhudi zao za Kuendelea), maadili na tabia. Matokeo Mauzo na Utangazaji, Mawasiliano ya pamoja ambapo tuliweza kuimarisha nafasi yake ni kwamba nembo ya KCB ilikua zaidi Kampuni na Uraia. Bernard na Rosalind yetu sokoni na kulinda maslahi ya wenyehisa. pamoja na matokeo yetu ya kifedha. Kundi wanaleta uzoefu wa miaka mingi katika sekta Vile vile, ningependa kutambua usaidizi na la KCB kwa sasa limefika hatua nyingine ya benki kulisaidia Kundi letu kufanikiwa uongozi ambao wasimamizi pamoja nami pia ya mabadiliko. Mazingira ya kibiashara hata zaidi. tumepokea kutoka kwa Bodi ya Wakurugenzi yanaendelea kubadilika, na ni lazima tunapojizatiti kuhakikisha Kundi la KCB tuendelee kubadilika nayo ili kutumia fursa Mustakabali wa 2022 linaendelea kufanikiwa hata zaidi katika mpya zinazotokea na pia kuendelea kuwa wa Kama Kundi, tumeweka mipango yetu na kanda hii. Nawashukuru wadau wetu wote maana kwa wateja wetu kama mtoaji huduma kuchagua maeneo yatakayoongoza shughuli kwa usaidizi wao na imani ambayo wamekuwa za kifedha anayependwa zaidi katika masoko zetu siku zijazo. Mkakati wa Zaidi ya Benki nayo kwangu, na Kamati Kuu Tendaji, katika tunayohudumu. Tumeanza kazi ya kuiboresha bado ndiyo nanga kwa biashara yetu. Jango la kuongoza Kundi la KCB. nembo yetu kuhakikisha tunajilainisha zaidi corona likiwa bado lipo na ukizingatia kwamba na mkakati na azma ya Zaidi ya Benki. ni mwaka wa uchaguzi Kenya, tuna matumaini ya kufanikiwa ingawa kwa tahadhari kuhusu Ajenda ya Watu mwaka huu. Hata hivyo, tunatarajia biashara Joshua Oigara, CBS Mafanikio yetu katika kipindi tunachoangazia yetu kuwa imara kutokana na kuimarika hayangewezekana bila bidii na kujitolea kwa kwa uchumi. Name: Bonnie Okumu Education and Professional Background: Date of appointment: (43 Years) March 2021 Bonnie Okumu is the Group General Counsel since January Designation: Company Secretary 2021. Prior to this, she was the Director, Legal Services appointed as such in July 2018 having been promoted from the role of Head, Legal Services which she held since January 2014 when she joined KCB. Before joining KCB, she was the Chief Legal and Regulatory Affairs Officer & Company Secretary at Telkom Kenya Limited. Prior to this she was the General Counsel & Company Secretary at Unilever Kenya Limited where she oversaw the legal and company secretarial functions for 9 operating companies in 7 countries in East and Southern Africa. Until she joined Unilever, she was the Regional Legal Manager for Nestle where she set up the legal department and led a team of lawyers in providing legal and tax advisory services to 14 operating entities in 20 countries in the Equatorial African Region. Earlier in her career, she was an associate at Dentons, Hamilton Harrison & Mathews and an audit assistant at Deloitte & Touché. She holds an LL.B from the University of Nairobi, is an advocate of the High Court of Kenya as well as a Certified Secretary (CS). 122

The calculation of the expected credit losses involves complex mathematical models that are prone to data integrity or configuration errors, or mathematical formulaic errors. This is an area of focus because of significant impact on the calculation of the expected credit losses: • the judgments made to determine the categorisation (staging) of individual loans and advances accounts in line with IFRS 9. In particular, the identification of Significant Increase in Credit Risk (“SICR”) and Default requires consideration of quantitative and qualitative criteria. data.item: Reliance on Information & Communications Technology systems for financial control and reporting. The Group’s financial control, accounting and reporting processes are heavily dependent on complex information & communications technology systems and applications. Specifically, the calculation, recording and financial reporting of financial transactions and balances are significantly dependent on automated processes. Weaknesses in the design and operating effectiveness of the automated accounting procedures and related IT dependent manual controls could result in material errors in the financial information, which makes this an area of focus. Our audit focus on information & communications technology systems and applications and controls over financial reporting included the following areas: Assessed and tested the design and operating effectiveness of the controls over the integrity of information technology (IT) systems and applications that are relevant for financial accounting and reporting. Tested controls over programs development and changes, access to programmes and data and IT operations including compensating controls where necessary. We also tested certain aspects of the security of the IT systems including logical access management and segregation of duties. Where, either design or operating effectiveness control deficiencies were identified, we altered our audit approach to test the compensating controls or increased the level of our tests of detail. These additional procedures mitigated the deficiencies or provided the additional audit

data.item: Amendment to IFRS 3, ‘Business combinations’ Asset or liability in a business combination clarity The Board has updated IFRS 3, ‘Business combinations’, to refer to the 2018 Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting, in order to determine what constitutes an asset or a liability in a business combination. In addition, the Board added a new exception in IFRS 3 for liabilities and contingent liabilities. The exception specifies that, for some types of liabilities and contingent liabilities, an entity applying IFRS 3 should instead refer to IAS 37, ‘Provisions, Contingent Liabilities and Contingent Assets’, or IFRIC 21, ‘Levies’, rather than the 2018 Conceptual Framework. The Board has also clarified that the acquirer should not recognise contingent assets, as defined in IAS 37, at the acquisition date. Annual periods beginning on or after 1 January 2022
